💡 Tip: Male parts = Stamen (Anther + Filament) · Female parts = Pistil (Stigma + Style + Ovary)

g.text: Stigma — green, sticky top of pistil
Style — green tube connecting stigma to ovary
Receptacle — swollen base, all parts attach here

g.text: 💡 Hints — Use These Clues to Identify Parts
Stigma — The sticky, knob-like tip at the very top of the pistil.
Petal — The large, colorful, leaf-like structures that attract pollinators.
Anther — The yellow, pollen-filled sac at the top of each stamen.
Stamen — The entire male reproductive organ (anther + filament).
Filament — The thin stalk that holds up the anther.
Pistil — The entire female reproductive organ (stigma + style + ovary).
Style — The slender tube connecting the stigma to the ovary.
Ovary — The enlarged base of the pistil containing ovules.
Sepal — Green, leaf-like structures beneath the petals; protect the bud.
Receptacle — The thickened area at the top of the stem where all parts attach.
Remember: Male parts make pollen · Female parts make seeds · Accessory parts help with pollination
• Confusing stamen (whole organ) with anther (just the tip)
• Confusing pistil (whole organ) with style (just the tube)
• Mixing up petal and sepal — remember sepals are green
• Placing receptacle too low — it's right at the base of the flower
"Some Boys Find All Girls Stylishly Outstanding"
Sepal · Boy (stamen) · Filament · Anther · Girl (pistil) · Style · Ovary
